summary: Ahead of the Chelsea vs Arsenal London derby, Mauricio Pochettino and Mikel Arteta spoke about their close bond dating back to Paris Saint-Germain in 2001, when Pochettino mentored the teenage Arteta. Both praised each other but said they will be fiercely competitive as head coaches meeting for the first time. The article also covers returning ex-Chelsea players Kai Havertz and Jorginho and team injury news for both clubs.
one_line: Pochettino and Arteta, close since their 2001 PSG days, prepare to face each other as head coaches in Chelsea vs Arsenal.
key_facts: Mauricio Pochettino and Mikel Arteta meet as head coaches for the first time on Saturday, when Arsenal visit Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.
In 2001 Arteta, a teenager, joined Paris Saint-Germain on loan from Barcelona's B side; Pochettino, 10 years older, took him under his wing.
Arteta and Pochettino lived together in a hotel for about three months in Paris.
Arteta says Pochettino was 'one of the most influential people in my career' and looked after him like a little brother.
Pochettino says Arteta 'was a coach already at 17' and can be one of the greatest managers in the world.
Pochettino says 'He's more than a friend - he's family' but wants to 'destroy the opponent' on matchday.
Arteta called Pochettino's early work at Chelsea 'phenomenal'.
Kai Havertz and Jorginho will return to Stamford Bridge for the first time since leaving Chelsea for Arsenal; Havertz has one goal in 12 Arsenal appearances.
Chelsea's Armando Broja will miss the game with 'irritation' in his knee; Reece James, Axel Disasi and Nicolas Jackson face late fitness checks, and Benoit Badiashile could return.
Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo should be available despite travelling to South America during the international break.
Chelsea remain without Ben Chilwell, Carney Chukwuemeka, Christopher Nkunku, Romeo Lavia, Wesley Fofana and Trevoh Chalobah.
Arsenal will make late calls on Bukayo Saka, William Saliba (chronic toe injury) and Leandro Trossard (hamstring).
Kick-off is 5.30pm on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Premier League from 5pm.
